title.raw: 卷10 志第5 禮儀五 Volume 10 Treatises 5: Rites 5

sentences.zh: 禮儀五

translations.literal: Rites, Part Five.
translations.idiomatic: Rites, Part Five

sentences.zh: 輿輦之別，蓋先王之所以列等威也。

translations.literal: The distinction between palanquins and sedan chairs—this is how the former kings arranged ranks and majesty.
translations.idiomatic: The distinction between palanquins and sedan chairs was how the ancient kings established ranks and displayed authority.

sentences.zh: 然隨時而變，代有不同。

translations.literal: Yet they changed with the times, and each age differed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet these arrangements changed with the times, and each dynasty had its own practices.

sentences.zh: 梁初尚遵齊制，其後武帝既議定禮儀，乃漸有變革。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Liang they still followed Qi regulations; afterward, once Emperor Wu had deliberated and fixed the rites, gradual reforms followed.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Liang dynasty the court still followed Qi regulations, but after Emperor Wu deliberated and established ritual protocol, gradual reforms began.

sentences.zh: 始永明中，步兵校尉伏曼容奏，宋大明中，尚書左丞荀萬秋議，金玉二輅，並建碧旂，象革木輅，並建赤旂，非時運所上，又非五方之色。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongming, Infantry Commandant Fu Manrong memorialized: in Song Daming, Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing Xun Wanqiu proposed that the jade and gold chariots both fly green banners, while the ivory, leather, and wood chariots both fly red banners—neither accorded with the color favored by the current dynastic fortune, nor with the colors of the five directions.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yongming, Infantry Commandant Fu Manrong submitted a memorial noting that in Song Daming, Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing Xun Wanqiu had proposed that the jade and gold chariots both carry green banners while the ivory, leather, and wood chariots both carry red banners—colors that neither matched the hue favored by the current dynastic fortune nor the colors of the five directions.

sentences.zh: 今五輅五牛及五色幡旗，並請准齊所尚青色。

translations.literal: Now for the five chariots, five oxen, and five-colored pennant flags, he requested that all follow Qi in honoring the color green.
translations.idiomatic: He now requested that the five chariots, five oxen, and five-colored pennant flags all follow Qi practice in honoring the color green.

sentences.zh: 時議所駁，不行。

translations.literal: The deliberation of the time rejected it, and it was not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: The deliberation of the time rejected the proposal, and it was not adopted.

sentences.zh: 及天監三年，乃改五輅旗同用赤而旒不異，以從行運所尚也。

translations.literal: By Tianjian 3, the banners of the five chariots were changed to use red uniformly while the tassels remained distinct, following the color favored by the current dynastic fortune.
translations.idiomatic: By Tianjian 3, the banners of the five chariots were changed to red uniformly while the tassels remained distinct, in accord with the color favored by the current dynastic fortune.

sentences.zh: 七年，帝曰：「據《禮》'玉輅以祀，金輅以賓'，而今大祀，並乘金輅。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, the emperor said: "According to the Rites, 'the jade chariot is for sacrifice; the gold chariot is for receiving guests'—yet today at the great sacrifices, all ride the gold chariot.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, the emperor said: "According to the Rites, 'the jade chariot is for sacrifice; the gold chariot is for receiving guests'—yet at the great sacrifices today, the emperor rides only the gold chariot.

sentences.zh: 」詔下詳議。

translations.literal: " An edict was issued for detailed deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued ordering detailed deliberation.

sentences.zh: 周舍以為：「金輅以之齋車，本不關於祭祀。

translations.literal: Zhou She held that: "The gold chariot serves as the fasting chariot and is not originally connected with sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou She argued: "The gold chariot serves as the fasting chariot and is not originally connected with sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 」於是改陵廟皆乘玉輅，大駕則太僕卿禦，法駕則奉車郎馭。

translations.literal: " Thereupon visits to the tombs and temples were changed to use the jade chariot; for the grand procession the Director of the Imperial Stud drove, and for the standard procession the Chariot Attendant drove.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon visits to imperial tombs and temples were changed to use the jade chariot; for the grand procession the Director of the Imperial Stud drove, and for the standard procession the Chariot Attendant drove.

sentences.zh: 其餘四輅，則使人執轡，以硃絲為之。

translations.literal: The remaining four chariots had men hold the reins, made of cinnabar silk.
translations.idiomatic: For the remaining four chariots, attendants held the reins, which were made of cinnabar silk.

sentences.zh: 執者武冠、硃衣。

translations.literal: Those who held them wore military caps and cinnabar robes.
translations.idiomatic: Those who held the reins wore military caps and cinnabar robes.

sentences.zh: 又齊永明制，玉輅上施重屋，棲寶鳳皇，綴金鈴，鑷珠璫、玉蚌佩。

translations.literal: Also under the Qi Yongming regulations, the jade chariot bore a double roof, with a jeweled phoenix perched upon it, gold bells suspended, pearl ear ornaments and jade clam-shell pendants attached.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Qi Yongming regulations as well, the jade chariot bore a double roof with a jeweled phoenix perched upon it, gold bells suspended, and pearl ear ornaments and jade clam-shell pendants attached.

sentences.zh: 四角金龍，銜五彩。

translations.literal: At the four corners were gold dragons holding five-colored streamers.
translations.idiomatic: At the four corners were gold dragons holding five-colored streamers.

sentences.zh: 又畫麒麟頭加于馬首者。

translations.literal: There were also painted qilin heads added to the horses' foreheads.
translations.idiomatic: Painted qilin heads were also added to the horses' foreheads.

sentences.zh: 十二年，帝皆省之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, the emperor abolished all of these.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, the emperor abolished all of these embellishments.

sentences.zh: 初，齊武帝造大小輦，並如軺車，但無輪轂，下橫轅軛。

translations.literal: At first, Qi Emperor Wu created large and small palanquins, both like light chariots but without wheel hubs, with cross shafts and yokes below.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, Qi Emperor Wu created large and small palanquins, both resembling light chariots but without wheel hubs, with cross shafts and yokes beneath.

sentences.zh: 梁初，漆畫代之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Liang, lacquer painting replaced them.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Liang, lacquer painting replaced these designs.

sentences.zh: 後帝令上可加笨輦，形如犢車，自茲始也。

translations.literal: Later the emperor ordered that a heavy palanquin could be added on top, shaped like a calf cart—this began from that time.
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor ordered that a heavy palanquin could be added on top, shaped like a calf cart—a practice that began at that time.

sentences.zh: 中方八尺，左右開四望。

translations.literal: The center was eight feet square; left and right had four open views.
translations.idiomatic: The center was eight feet square, with four open views on the left and right.

sentences.zh: 金為龍首。

translations.literal: Gold formed the dragon head.
translations.idiomatic: The dragon head was made of gold.

sentences.zh: 飾其五末，謂轅轂頭及衡端也。

translations.literal: The five ends were decorated—that is, the shaft ends, hub ends, and crossbar ends.
translations.idiomatic: The five ends were decorated—that is, the shaft ends, hub ends, and crossbar ends.

sentences.zh: 金鸞棲軛。

translations.literal: A gold luan bird perched on the yoke.
translations.idiomatic: A gold luan bird perched on the yoke.

sentences.zh: 其下施重層，以空青雕鏤為龍鳳象。

translations.literal: Below it were layered tiers, with dragons, phoenixes, and elephants carved and inlaid in azurite.
translations.idiomatic: Below it were layered tiers with dragons, phoenixes, and elephants carved and inlaid in azurite.

sentences.zh: 漆木橫前，名為望板。

translations.literal: A lacquered wooden crossbeam ran across the front, called the viewing board.
translations.idiomatic: A lacquered wooden crossbeam ran across the front, called the viewing board.

sentences.zh: 其下交施三十六橫。

translations.literal: Below it thirty-six crossbars were interlaced.
translations.idiomatic: Below it thirty-six crossbars were interlaced.

sentences.zh: 小輿形似軺車，金裝漆畫，但施八橫。

translations.literal: The small palanquin resembled a light chariot, with gold fittings and lacquer painting, but had only eight crossbars.
translations.idiomatic: The small palanquin resembled a light chariot with gold fittings and lacquer painting, but had only eight crossbars.

sentences.zh: 元正大會，乘出上殿。

translations.literal: At the New Year's grand assembly, one rode it out to ascend the hall.
translations.idiomatic: At the New Year's grand assembly, the emperor rode it out to ascend the hall.

sentences.zh: 西堂舉哀亦乘之。

translations.literal: At mourning rites in the Western Hall one also rode it.
translations.idiomatic: At mourning rites in the Western Hall the emperor also rode it.

sentences.zh: 行則從後。

translations.literal: When traveling, it followed behind.
translations.idiomatic: When traveling, it followed behind.

sentences.zh: 一名輿車。

translations.literal: It was also called the palanquin carriage.
translations.idiomatic: It was also called the palanquin carriage.

sentences.zh: 羊車一名輦，其上如軺，小兒衣青布袴褶，五辮髻，數人引之。

translations.literal: The sheep cart was also called a palanquin; above it was like a light chariot; small boys wore blue cloth trousers and jackets, with five braided topknots, and several men pulled it.
translations.idiomatic: The sheep cart, also called a palanquin, had an upper structure like a light chariot; small boys in blue cloth trousers and jackets with five braided topknots pulled it.

sentences.zh: 時名羊車小史。

translations.literal: At the time it was called the sheep-cart attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At the time it was called the sheep-cart attendant.

sentences.zh: 漢氏或以人牽，或駕果下馬。

translations.literal: Under the Han dynasty, sometimes men pulled it, or sometimes it was drawn by short horses.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Han dynasty, it was sometimes pulled by men and sometimes drawn by short horses.

sentences.zh: 梁貴賤通得乘之，名曰牽子。

translations.literal: In Liang both noble and common could ride it; it was called the hand-drawn cart.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang both nobles and commoners could ride it; it was called the hand-drawn cart.

sentences.zh: 畫輪車，一乘，駕牛。

translations.literal: The painted-wheel cart: one carriage, drawn by oxen.
translations.idiomatic: The painted-wheel cart: one carriage, drawn by oxen.

sentences.zh: 乘用如齊制，舊史言之詳矣。

translations.literal: Its use followed Qi regulations; the old histories describe it in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Its use followed Qi regulations; the old histories describe it in detail.

sentences.zh: 衣書車，十二乘，駕牛。

translations.literal: The robe-and-scroll cart: twelve carriages, drawn by oxen.
translations.idiomatic: The robe-and-scroll cart: twelve carriages, drawn by oxen.

sentences.zh: 漢皁蓋硃裏，過江加綠油幢。

translations.literal: Under the Han it had a black canopy and cinnabar lining; after crossing the Yangtze a green-oil banner was added.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Han it had a black canopy and cinnabar lining; after the court crossed the Yangtze a green-oil banner was added.

sentences.zh: 硃絲絡，青交路，黃金塗五末。

translations.literal: Cinnabar silk netting, green cross-pattern trim, and gold plating on the five ends.
translations.idiomatic: It had cinnabar silk netting, green cross-pattern trim, and gold plating on the five ends.

sentences.zh: 一曰副車。

translations.literal: It was also called the secondary carriage.
translations.idiomatic: It was also called the secondary carriage.

sentences.zh: 梁朝謂之衣書車。

translations.literal: The Liang dynasty called it the robe-and-scroll cart.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang dynasty called it the robe-and-scroll cart.

sentences.zh: 皇太子鸞輅，駕三馬，左右騑。

translations.literal: The crown prince's luan chariot was drawn by three horses with outriders left and right.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's luan chariot was drawn by three horses with outriders on the left and right.

sentences.zh: 硃斑輪，倚獸較，伏鹿軾，九旒，畫降龍，青蓋畫幡，文輈，黃金塗五末。

translations.literal: Cinnabar-spotted wheels, beast-shaped side rails, a recumbent deer on the front rail, nine tassels, painted descending dragons, a green canopy with painted banners, patterned shafts, and gold plating on the five ends.
translations.idiomatic: It had cinnabar-spotted wheels, beast-shaped side rails, a recumbent deer on the front rail, nine tassels, painted descending dragons, a green canopy with painted banners, patterned shafts, and gold plating on the five ends.

sentences.zh: 近代亦謂之鸞輅，即象蓋也。

translations.literal: In recent times it was also called the luan chariot—that is, the ivory-canopied chariot.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times it was also called the luan chariot—that is, the ivory-canopied chariot.

sentences.zh: 梁東宮初建及太子釋奠、元正朝會則乘之。

translations.literal: In Liang, when the Eastern Palace was first established, and at the crown prince's libation ceremony and New Year's court assembly, he rode it.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang, when the Eastern Palace was first established and at the crown prince's libation ceremony and New Year's court assembly, he rode it.

sentences.zh: 以畫輪為副。

translations.literal: The painted-wheel cart served as secondary.
translations.idiomatic: The painted-wheel cart served as the secondary carriage.

sentences.zh: 若常乘畫輪，以軺衣書車為副。

translations.literal: If he regularly rode the painted-wheel cart, the light chariot and robe-and-scroll cart served as secondary.
translations.idiomatic: If he regularly rode the painted-wheel cart, the light chariot and robe-and-scroll cart served as secondary carriages.

sentences.zh: 畫輪車，上開四望，綠油幢，硃繩絡，兩箱裏飾以錦，黃金塗五末。

translations.literal: The painted-wheel cart had four open views above, a green-oil banner, cinnabar rope netting, both compartments lined with brocade, and gold plating on the five ends.
translations.idiomatic: The painted-wheel cart had four open views above, a green-oil banner, cinnabar rope netting, both compartments lined with brocade, and gold plating on the five ends.

sentences.zh: 二千石四品已上及列侯，皆給軺車，駕牛。

translations.literal: Officials of two thousand bushels, fourth rank and above, and enfeoffed marquises all received light chariots drawn by oxen.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of two thousand bushels, fourth rank and above, and enfeoffed marquises all received light chariots drawn by oxen.

sentences.zh: 伏兔箱，青油幢，硃絲絡，轂輞皆黑漆。

translations.literal: Recumbent rabbit on the box, green-oil banner, cinnabar silk netting, and hub rims all lacquered black.
translations.idiomatic: They had a recumbent rabbit on the box, green-oil banner, cinnabar silk netting, and hub rims all lacquered black.

sentences.zh: 天監二年令，三公、開府、尚書令，則給鹿幡軺，施耳，後戶，皁輞。

translations.literal: The Tianjian 2 decree: for the Three Excellencies, those who opened a government office, and the Director of the Masters of Writing, deer-banner light chariots were provided, with ear fittings, rear doors, and black hub rims.
translations.idiomatic: The Tianjian 2 decree stipulated that the Three Excellencies, those who opened a government office, and the Director of the Masters of Writing received deer-banner light chariots with ear fittings, rear doors, and black hub rims.

sentences.zh: 尚書僕射、左右光祿大夫、侍中、中書監令、秘書監，則給鳳轄軺，後戶，皁輞。

translations.literal: For the Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Left and Right Masters of Brilliant Happiness, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Director and Vice Director of the Palace Library and Secretariat, and Director of the Palace Library, phoenix-shaft light chariots were provided, with rear doors and black hub rims.
translations.idiomatic: For the Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, the Left and Right Masters of Brilliant Happiness, the Attendant-in-Ordinary, the Director and Vice Director of the Secretariat, and the Director of the Palace Library, phoenix-shaft light chariots with rear doors and black hub rims were provided.

sentences.zh: 領、護、國子祭酒、太子詹事、尚書、侍中、列卿、散騎常侍，給聊泥軺，無後戶，漆輪。

translations.literal: For Directors, Guardians, Director of the Imperial Academy, Grand Steward of the Heir Apparent, Masters of Writing, Attendants-in-Ordinary, chief ministers, and Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, lacquered-mud light chariots were provided, without rear doors, with lacquered wheels.
translations.idiomatic: For Directors, Guardians, the Director of the Imperial Academy, the Grand Steward of the Heir Apparent, Masters of Writing, Attendants-in-Ordinary, chief ministers, and Regular Attendants of the Cavalry, lacquered-mud light chariots without rear doors and with lacquered wheels were provided.

sentences.zh: 車騎、驃騎及諸王除刺史、帶將軍，給龍雀軺，以金銀飾。

translations.literal: Masters of Cavalry, Masters of Fast Cavalry, and all princes except when serving as regional inspectors or bearing general's titles received dragon-sparrow light chariots decorated with gold and silver.
translations.idiomatic: Masters of Cavalry, Masters of Fast Cavalry, and all princes except when serving as regional inspectors or bearing general's titles received dragon-sparrow light chariots decorated with gold and silver.

sentences.zh: 禦史中丞給方蓋軺，形如小傘。

translations.literal: The Inspector of the Masters of Writing received a square-canopy light chariot, shaped like a small umbrella.
translations.idiomatic: The Inspector of the Masters of Writing received a square-canopy light chariot shaped like a small umbrella.

sentences.zh: 諸王三公有勳德者，皆特加皁輪車，駕牛，形如犢車。

translations.literal: Princes and the Three Excellencies who had merit and virtue all received black-wheeled carts in addition, drawn by oxen, shaped like calf carts.
translations.idiomatic: Princes and members of the Three Excellencies who had merit and virtue all additionally received black-wheeled carts drawn by oxen, shaped like calf carts.

sentences.zh: 但烏漆輪轂，黃金雕裝，上加青油幢，硃絲絡，通幰或四望。

translations.literal: But with black-lacquered wheel hubs, gold carved fittings, a green-oil banner above, cinnabar silk netting, and either full canopy or four open views.
translations.idiomatic: They had black-lacquered wheel hubs, gold carved fittings, a green-oil banner above, cinnabar silk netting, and either a full canopy or four open views.

sentences.zh: 上臺，三夫人亦乘之，以拓幢涅幰為副。

translations.literal: When ascending the upper platform, the three consorts also rode them, with banner-and-dark-canopy carts as secondary.
translations.idiomatic: When ascending the upper platform, the three consorts also rode them, with banner-and-dark-canopy carts as secondary carriages.

sentences.zh: 王公加禮者，給油幢絡車，駕牛。

translations.literal: Princes and dukes who received additional honors were given oil-banner netted carts drawn by oxen.
translations.idiomatic: Princes and dukes who received additional honors were given oil-banner netted carts drawn by oxen.

sentences.zh: 硃輪華轂。

translations.literal: Cinnabar wheels and ornate hubs.
translations.idiomatic: They had cinnabar wheels and ornate hubs.

sentences.zh: 天監二年令，上臺，六宮、長公主、公主、諸王太妃、妃，皆乘青油輿幢車通幰車，拓幢涅幰為副。

translations.literal: The Tianjian 2 decree: when ascending the upper platform, the six palaces, grand princesses, princesses, grand consorts and consorts of princes all rode green-oil banner-and-canopy carts or full-canopy carts, with banner-and-dark-canopy carts as secondary.
translations.idiomatic: The Tianjian 2 decree stipulated that when ascending the upper platform, the six palaces, grand princesses, princesses, and grand consorts and consorts of princes all rode green-oil banner-and-canopy carts or full-canopy carts, with banner-and-dark-canopy carts as secondary carriages.

sentences.zh: 采女、皇女、諸王嗣子、侯夫人，皆乘赤油拓幢車，以涅幰為副。

translations.literal: Selected palace women, imperial daughters, heirs of princes, and consorts of marquises all rode red-oil banner carts, with dark-canopy carts as secondary.
translations.idiomatic: Selected palace women, imperial daughters, heirs of princes, and consorts of marquises all rode red-oil banner carts, with dark-canopy carts as secondary carriages.

sentences.zh: 侍女、直乘涅幰之乘。

translations.literal: Attendant women and those on regular duty rode dark-canopy carriages.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant women and those on regular duty rode dark-canopy carriages.

sentences.zh: 諸王三公並乘通幰平乘車，竹箕子壁、仰，郐資榆為輞。

translations.literal: All princes and the Three Excellencies rode full-canopy flat carriages, with bamboo basket walls and upward-curving sides, and elm hub rims.
translations.idiomatic: All princes and the Three Excellencies rode full-canopy flat carriages with bamboo basket walls and upward-curving sides and elm hub rims.

sentences.zh: 如今犢車，但舉幰通覆上。

translations.literal: Like calf carts today, but with the canopy raised to cover the top entirely.
translations.idiomatic: They resembled today's calf carts, but with the canopy raised to cover the top entirely.

sentences.zh: 方州刺史，並乘通幰平肩輿，從橫施八橫，亦得金渡裝較。

translations.literal: Regional inspectors all rode full-canopy flat-shouldered palanquins, with eight crossbars arranged horizontally, and could also have gold-plated side rails.
translations.idiomatic: Regional inspectors all rode full-canopy flat-shouldered palanquins with eight crossbars arranged horizontally and could also have gold-plated side rails.

sentences.zh: 天子至於下賤，通乘步輿，方四尺，上施隱膝以及襻，舉之。

translations.literal: From the Son of Heaven down to the lowest ranks, all could ride hand-carried palanquins, four feet square, with hidden knee-rests and carrying straps added above, and be lifted.
translations.idiomatic: From the Son of Heaven down to the lowest ranks, all could ride hand-carried palanquins four feet square, fitted with hidden knee-rests and carrying straps above, and be lifted by bearers.

sentences.zh: 無禁限。

translations.literal: There were no prohibitions or limits.
translations.idiomatic: There were no prohibitions or limits on their use.

sentences.zh: 載輿亦如之，但不施腳，以其就席便也。

translations.literal: Transport palanquins were the same, but without legs, for convenience when taking one's seat.
translations.idiomatic: Transport palanquins were the same, but without legs, for convenience when taking one's seat.

sentences.zh: 優禮者，人輿以升殿。

translations.literal: Those granted special honors were carried in palanquins to ascend the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Those granted special honors were carried in palanquins to ascend the hall.

sentences.zh: 司徒謝朏，以腳疾優之。

translations.literal: Grand Minister Xie Tiao was granted this honor because of a foot ailment.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Minister Xie Tiao was granted this honor because of a foot ailment.

sentences.zh: 五牛旗，左青赤，右白黑，黃居其中，蓋古之五時副車也。

translations.literal: The Five Ox Banners: on the left green and red, on the right white and black, with yellow in the center—this was the ancient five-season secondary carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Ox Banners: on the left green and red, on the right white and black, with yellow in the center—this was the ancient five-season secondary carriage.

sentences.zh: 舊有五色立車，五色安車，合十乘，名為五時車。

translations.literal: Formerly there were five-colored standing carriages and five-colored secure carriages, ten in all, called the five-season carriages.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly there were five-colored standing carriages and five-colored secure carriages, ten in all, called the five-season carriages.

sentences.zh: 建旗十二，各如車色。

translations.literal: Twelve banners were erected, each matching the color of its carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve banners were erected, each matching the color of its carriage.

sentences.zh: 立車則正豎其旗，安車則斜注。

translations.literal: On standing carriages the banners stood upright; on secure carriages they slanted.
translations.idiomatic: On standing carriages the banners stood upright; on secure carriages they slanted.

sentences.zh: 馬亦隨五時之色，白馬則硃其鬣尾。

translations.literal: The horses also followed the colors of the five seasons; white horses had their manes and tails dyed cinnabar.
translations.idiomatic: The horses also followed the colors of the five seasons; white horses had their manes and tails dyed cinnabar.

sentences.zh: 左右騑驂，金鍰鏤錫，黃屋左纛，如金根之制。

translations.literal: Outriders left and right as escorts, with gold ringed and engraved bits, yellow canopy and left banner streamer, following the regulations of the gold-root carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Outriders served as escorts left and right, with gold ringed and engraved bits, yellow canopy and left banner streamer, following the regulations of the gold-root carriage.

sentences.zh: 行則從後。

translations.literal: When traveling, they followed behind.
translations.idiomatic: When traveling, they followed behind.

sentences.zh: 名五時副車。

translations.literal: They were called the five-season secondary carriages.
translations.idiomatic: They were called the five-season secondary carriages.

sentences.zh: 晉過江，不恆有事，則權以馬車代之，建旗其上。

translations.literal: After Jin crossed the Yangtze, when there were not always occasions for them, horse carriages were temporarily substituted, with banners erected upon them.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin crossed the Yangtze, when there were not always occasions requiring them, horse carriages were temporarily substituted with banners erected upon them.

sentences.zh: 後但以五色木牛象車，豎旗于牛背，使人輿之。

translations.literal: Later they used only five-colored wooden ox effigy carts, with banners erected on the oxen's backs, and men carried them in palanquins.
translations.idiomatic: Later they used only five-colored wooden ox effigy carts with banners erected on the oxen's backs, carried by men in palanquins.

sentences.zh: 旗常纏不舒，唯天子親戎，乃舒其旆。

translations.literal: The banners were usually furled and not unfurled; only when the Son of Heaven personally took the field were the pennants spread.
translations.idiomatic: The banners were usually furled and not unfurled; only when the Son of Heaven personally took the field were the pennants spread.

sentences.zh: 周遷以為晉武帝平吳後造五牛之旗，非過江始為也。

translations.literal: Zhou Qian held that the Five Ox Banners were made after Jin Emperor Wu pacified Wu, and were not first created after crossing the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Qian held that the Five Ox Banners were made after Jin Emperor Wu pacified Wu and were not first created after crossing the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 指南車，大駕出，為先啟之乘。

translations.literal: The south-pointing chariot: when the grand procession set out, it was the leading carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The south-pointing chariot: when the grand procession set out, it was the leading carriage.

sentences.zh: 漢初，置俞兒騎，並為先驅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han, the Yu'er Cavalry was established, and both served as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Han, the Yu'er Cavalry was established, and both served as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 左太沖曰：「俞騎騁路，指南司方。

translations.literal: Left Tai Chong wrote: "The Yu riders gallop the road; the south-pointer governs direction.
translations.idiomatic: Left Tai Chong wrote: "The Yu riders gallop the road; the south-pointer governs direction.

sentences.zh: 」後廢其騎而存其車。

translations.literal: " Later the cavalry was abolished but the chariot was retained.
translations.idiomatic: " Later the cavalry was abolished but the chariot was retained.

sentences.zh: 記裏車，駕牛。

translations.literal: The distance-recording chariot, drawn by oxen.
translations.idiomatic: The distance-recording chariot, drawn by oxen.

sentences.zh: 其中有木人執槌，車行一裏，則打一槌。

translations.literal: Inside it a wooden figure held a mallet; when the chariot traveled one li, it struck one blow.
translations.idiomatic: Inside it a wooden figure held a mallet; when the chariot traveled one li, it struck one blow.

sentences.zh: 鼓吹車，上施層樓，四角金龍，銜旒蘇羽葆。

translations.literal: The drum-and-pipe chariot had layered towers above, with gold dragons at the four corners holding tasseled feather canopies.
translations.idiomatic: The drum-and-pipe chariot had layered towers above, with gold dragons at the four corners holding tasseled feather canopies.

sentences.zh: 凡鼓吹，陸則樓車，水則樓船，在殿庭則畫筍虡為樓。

translations.literal: For all drum-and-pipe music: on land there was the tower chariot, on water the tower ship, and in the palace courtyard painted bamboo frames served as towers.
translations.idiomatic: For all drum-and-pipe music: on land there was the tower chariot, on water the tower ship, and in the palace courtyard painted bamboo frames served as towers.

sentences.zh: 樓上有翔鷺棲烏，或為鵠形。

translations.literal: On the tower were soaring herons and perched crows, or sometimes swan shapes.
translations.idiomatic: On the tower were soaring herons and perched crows, or sometimes swan shapes.

sentences.zh: 陳承梁末，王琳縱火，延燒車府。

translations.literal: Chen inherited the end of Liang; Wang Lin set fire and burned the carriage depot.
translations.idiomatic: Chen inherited the end of Liang; Wang Lin set fire and burned the carriage depot.

sentences.zh: 至天嘉元年，敕守都官尚書、寶安侯到仲舉，議造玉金象革木等五輅及五色副車。

translations.literal: By Tiancheng 1, an edict ordered the Guardian Director of the Masters of Writing, Marquis Dao Zhongju of Bao'an, to deliberate on constructing the five chariots of jade, gold, ivory, leather, and wood, and the five-colored secondary carriages.
translations.idiomatic: By Tiancheng 1, an edict ordered the Guardian Director of the Masters of Writing, Marquis Dao Zhongju of Bao'an, to deliberate on constructing the five chariots of jade, gold, ivory, leather, and wood and the five-colored secondary carriages.

sentences.zh: 皆金薄交龍，為輿倚較，文貔伏軾，虯首銜軛，左右吉陽筒，鸞雀立衡，郐虡文畫轓，綠油蓋，黃絞裏，相思郐愰，金華末。

translations.literal: All had gold-leaf interlaced dragons as carriage side rails, patterned leopard figures recumbent on the front rail, horned dragon heads holding the yoke, auspicious tubes left and right, luan sparrows standing on the crossbar, patterned elm side boards, green-oil canopy, yellow silk lining, paired acacia bells, and gold flower ends.
translations.idiomatic: All had gold-leaf interlaced dragons as carriage side rails, patterned leopard figures recumbent on the front rail, horned dragon heads holding the yoke, auspicious tubes left and right, luan sparrows standing on the crossbar, patterned elm side boards, green-oil canopy, yellow silk lining, paired acacia bells, and gold flower ends.

sentences.zh: 斜注旂旗于車之左，各依方色。

translations.literal: Slanting pennant flags were placed on the left of each chariot, each according to its directional color.
translations.idiomatic: Slanting pennant flags were placed on the left of each chariot, each according to its directional color.

sentences.zh: 加棨戟于車之右，韜以黻繡之衣。

translations.literal: Halberds were added on the right of each chariot, sheathed in robes embroidered with fu patterns.
translations.idiomatic: Halberds were added on the right of each chariot, sheathed in robes embroidered with fu patterns.

sentences.zh: 獸頭幡，長丈四尺，懸於戟杪。

translations.literal: The beast-head banner, one zhang and four chi in length, suspended at the tip of the halberd.
translations.idiomatic: The beast-head banner, one zhang and four chi in length, was suspended at the tip of the halberd.

sentences.zh: 玉輅，正副同駕六馬，餘輅皆駕四馬。

translations.literal: The jade chariot: the principal and secondary both drew six horses; the remaining chariots all drew four horses.
translations.idiomatic: For the jade chariot, the principal and secondary carriages both drew six horses; the remaining chariots all drew four horses.

sentences.zh: 馬並黃金為文髦，插以翟尾，玉為鏤錫。

translations.literal: The horses all had patterned manes of gold, with pheasant tails inserted, and jade engraved bits.
translations.idiomatic: The horses all had patterned manes of gold, with pheasant tails inserted and jade engraved bits.

sentences.zh: 又以彩畫赤油，長三尺，廣八寸，系兩軸頭，古曰飛軨，改以彩畫蛙蟆幡，綴兩軸頭，即古飛軨遺象也。

translations.literal: Also painted cinnabar oil, three chi long and eight cun wide, attached to both axle ends—the ancients called it flying fender; it was changed to painted toad banners attached to both axle ends, preserving the ancient flying-fender form.
translations.idiomatic: Also painted cinnabar oil, three chi long and eight cun wide, was attached to both axle ends—the ancients called this the flying fender; it was changed to painted toad banners attached to both axle ends, preserving the ancient flying-fender form.

sentences.zh: 五輅兩箱後，皆用玳瑁為鶤翅，加以金銀雕飾，故俗人謂之金鶤車。

translations.literal: Behind both compartments of the five chariots, tortoiseshell was used for kun wings, with gold and silver carved ornament, so common people called them gold-kun chariots.
translations.idiomatic: Behind both compartments of the five chariots, tortoiseshell was used for kun wings with gold and silver carved ornament, so common people called them gold-kun chariots.

sentences.zh: 兩箱之裏，衣以紅錦，金花帖釘，上用紅紫錦為後簷，青絞純帶，夏用簟，冬用綺繡褥。

translations.literal: The interiors of both compartments were lined with red brocade, with gold-flower nail studs; red and purple brocade served as the rear eaves; green cross-pattern pure sashes; bamboo mats in summer and brocade quilts in winter.
translations.idiomatic: The interiors of both compartments were lined with red brocade with gold-flower nail studs; red and purple brocade served as the rear eaves; green cross-pattern sashes were used; bamboo mats in summer and brocade quilts in winter.

sentences.zh: 此後漸修，具依梁制。

translations.literal: After this they were gradually refined, all following Liang regulations.
translations.idiomatic: After this they were gradually refined, all following Liang regulations.

sentences.zh: 後魏天興初，詔儀曹郎董謐撰朝饗儀，始制軒冕，未知古式，多違舊章。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianxing in Later Wei, an edict ordered Director of Ritual Affairs Dong Mi to compile court feast rites and first establish carriage caps and robes; not knowing the ancient forms, many violated old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianxing in Later Wei, an edict ordered Director of Ritual Affairs Dong Mi to compile court feast rites and first establish carriage caps and robes; not knowing the ancient forms, many provisions violated old regulations.

sentences.zh: 孝文帝時，儀曹令李韶更奏詳定，討論經籍，議改正之。

translations.literal: During Emperor Xiaowen's reign, Director of Ritual Affairs Li Shao memorialized again for detailed determination, examining the classics and deliberating corrections.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Xiaowen's reign, Director of Ritual Affairs Li Shao memorialized again for detailed determination, examining the classics and deliberating on corrections.

sentences.zh: 唯備五輅，各依方色，其餘車輦，猶未能具。

translations.literal: Only the five chariots were prepared, each according to its directional color; the remaining carriages and palanquins could not yet be fully supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Only the five chariots were prepared, each according to its directional color; the remaining carriages and palanquins could not yet be fully supplied.

sentences.zh: 至熙平九年，明帝又詔侍中崔光與安豐王延明、博士崔瓚采其議，大造車服。

translations.literal: By Xiping 9, Emperor Ming again ordered Attendant-in-Ordinary Cui Guang, together with Prince Yanming of Anfeng and Erudite Cui Zan, to adopt their deliberations and greatly manufacture carriages and robes.
translations.idiomatic: By Xiping 9, Emperor Ming again ordered Attendant-in-Ordinary Cui Guang, together with Prince Yanming of Anfeng and Erudite Cui Zan, to adopt their deliberations and greatly manufacture carriages and robes.

sentences.zh: 定制，五輅並駕五馬。

translations.literal: Regulations were fixed: the five chariots all drew five horses.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations were fixed: the five chariots all drew five horses.

sentences.zh: 皇太子乘金輅，硃蓋赤質，四馬。

translations.literal: The crown prince rode the gold chariot, with cinnabar canopy and red body, four horses.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince rode the gold chariot with a cinnabar canopy and red body, drawn by four horses.

sentences.zh: 三公及王，硃屋青表，制同於輅，名曰高車，駕三馬。

translations.literal: The Three Excellencies and princes had cinnabar roof and green exterior, regulations the same as the chariots, called high carriages, drawn by three horses.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Excellencies and princes had cinnabar roof and green exterior, regulations the same as the chariots, called high carriages, drawn by three horses.

sentences.zh: 庶姓王、侯及尚書令、僕已下，列卿已上，並給軺車，駕用一馬。

translations.literal: Princes of non-imperial surname, marquises, and from the Director of the Masters of Writing and Vice Director downward to chief ministers and above all received light chariots, drawn by one horse.
translations.idiomatic: Princes of non-imperial surname, marquises, and from the Director of the Masters of Writing and Vice Director downward to chief ministers and above all received light chariots drawn by one horse.

sentences.zh: 或乘四望通幰車，駕一牛。

translations.literal: Or they rode four-view full-canopy carriages, drawn by one ox.
translations.idiomatic: Or they rode four-view full-canopy carriages drawn by one ox.

sentences.zh: 自斯以後，條章粗備，北齊鹹取用焉。

translations.literal: From then on the regulations were roughly complete, and Northern Qi all adopted them.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the regulations were roughly complete, and Northern Qi adopted them in full.

sentences.zh: 其後因而著令，並無增損。

translations.literal: Later they were incorporated into statutes accordingly, with no additions or reductions.
translations.idiomatic: Later they were incorporated into statutes accordingly, with no additions or reductions.

sentences.zh: 王、庶姓王、儀同三司已上、親公主，雉尾扇，紫傘。

translations.literal: Princes, princes of non-imperial surname, those of Equal to the Three Excellencies and above, and imperial princesses: pheasant-tail fans and purple umbrellas.
translations.idiomatic: Princes, princes of non-imperial surname, those of Equal to the Three Excellencies and above, and imperial princesses received pheasant-tail fans and purple umbrellas.

sentences.zh: 皇宗及三品已上官，青傘硃裏。

translations.literal: Imperial clansmen and officials of third rank and above: green umbrellas with cinnabar lining.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial clansmen and officials of third rank and above received green umbrellas with cinnabar lining.

sentences.zh: 其青傘碧裏，達于士人，不禁。

translations.literal: Green umbrellas with green lining extended to commoners; there was no prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: Green umbrellas with green lining extended to commoners; there was no prohibition.

sentences.zh: 正從第一品執事官、散官及儀同三司、諸公主，得乘油色硃絡網車，車牛飾得用金塗及純銀。

translations.literal: Regular and concurrent first-rank active officials, honorary officials, those Equal to the Three Excellencies, and all princesses could ride oil-colored cinnabar netted carriages; carriage and ox fittings could use gold plating and pure silver.
translations.idiomatic: Regular and concurrent first-rank active officials, honorary officials, those Equal to the Three Excellencies, and all princesses could ride oil-colored cinnabar netted carriages; carriage and ox fittings could use gold plating and pure silver.

sentences.zh: 二品、三品得乘卷通幰車，車牛飾用金塗。

translations.literal: Second and third ranks could ride rolled full-canopy carriages; carriage and ox fittings used gold plating.
translations.idiomatic: Second and third ranks could ride rolled full-canopy carriages; carriage and ox fittings used gold plating.

sentences.zh: 四品已下，七品已上，得乘偏幰車，車牛飾用銅。

translations.literal: Fourth rank and below, seventh rank and above, could ride partial-canopy carriages; carriage and ox fittings used copper.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth rank and below, seventh rank and above, could ride partial-canopy carriages; carriage and ox fittings used copper.

sentences.zh: 尚書令給哄士十五人，左右僕射、禦史中丞，各十二人。

translations.literal: The Director of the Masters of Writing was given fifteen attendants; the Left and Right Vice Directors and the Inspector of the Masters of Writing each received twelve.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Masters of Writing was given fifteen attendants; the Left and Right Vice Directors and the Inspector of the Masters of Writing each received twelve.

sentences.zh: 周氏設六官，置司輅之職，以掌公車之政，辨其名品，與其物色。

translations.literal: The Zhou dynasty established six offices and created the office of Director of Chariots to manage public carriage affairs, distinguishing their names, ranks, and fittings.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou dynasty established six offices and created the office of Director of Chariots to manage public carriage affairs, distinguishing their names, ranks, and fittings.

sentences.zh: 皇帝之輅，十有二等：一曰蒼輅，以祀昊天上帝。

translations.literal: The emperor's chariots numbered twelve grades: first, the dark chariot, for sacrificing to the Supreme God of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's chariots numbered twelve grades: first, the dark chariot, for sacrificing to the Supreme God of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 二曰青輅，以祀東方上帝。

translations.literal: Second, the green chariot, for sacrificing to the God of the East.
translations.idiomatic: Second, the green chariot, for sacrificing to the God of the East.

sentences.zh: 三曰硃輅，以祀南方上帝及朝日。

translations.literal: Third, the cinnabar chariot, for sacrificing to the God of the South and the morning sun.
translations.idiomatic: Third, the cinnabar chariot, for sacrificing to the God of the South and the morning sun.

sentences.zh: 四曰黃輅，以祭地祇中央上帝。

translations.literal: Fourth, the yellow chariot, for sacrificing to the Earth and the Central God.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, the yellow chariot, for sacrificing to the Earth and the Central God.

sentences.zh: 五曰白輅，以祀西方上帝及夕月。

translations.literal: Fifth, the white chariot, for sacrificing to the God of the West and the evening moon.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, the white chariot, for sacrificing to the God of the West and the evening moon.

sentences.zh: 六曰玄輅，以祀北方上帝及感帝，祭神州。

translations.literal: Sixth, the black chariot, for sacrificing to the God of the North and the Lord of Felt, and for sacrificing to the Nine Regions.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth, the black chariot, for sacrificing to the God of the North and the Lord of Felt, and for sacrificing to the Nine Regions.

sentences.zh: 此六輅，通漆之而已，不用他物為飾。

translations.literal: These six chariots were simply lacquered throughout, without using other materials for ornament.
translations.idiomatic: These six chariots were simply lacquered throughout, without using other materials for ornament.

sentences.zh: 皆疏面，旒就以方色，俱十有二。

translations.literal: All had open faces; the tassel ornaments followed the directional colors, twelve in all.
translations.idiomatic: All had open faces; the tassel ornaments followed the directional colors, twelve in all.

sentences.zh: 疏面，刻皮當顱。

translations.literal: Open face: leather carved at the forehead.
translations.idiomatic: Open face: leather carved at the forehead.

sentences.zh: 七曰玉輅，以享先皇，加元服，納後。

translations.literal: Seventh, the jade chariot, for feasting the former emperors, conferring the capping ceremony, and receiving the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh, the jade chariot, for feasting the former emperors, conferring the capping ceremony, and receiving the empress.

sentences.zh: 八曰碧輅，以祭社稷，享諸先帝，大貞於龜，食三老五更，享食諸侯及耕籍。

translations.literal: Eighth, the jade-green chariot, for sacrificing to the altars of soil and grain, feasting the former emperors, great divination with tortoise, feeding the three elders and five worthies, feasting enfeoffed lords, and plowing the sacred field.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth, the jade-green chariot, for sacrificing to the altars of soil and grain, feasting the former emperors, great divination with tortoise, feeding the three elders and five worthies, feasting enfeoffed lords, and plowing the sacred field.

sentences.zh: 九曰金輅，以祀星辰，祭四望，視朔，大射，賓射，饗群臣，巡犧牲，養國老。

translations.literal: Ninth, the gold chariot, for sacrificing to the stars, sacrificing to the four mountain-waters, viewing the new moon, great archery, guest archery, feasting the ministers, inspecting sacrificial animals, and nurturing the state elders.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth, the gold chariot, for sacrificing to the stars, sacrificing to the four mountain-waters, viewing the new moon, great archery, guest archery, feasting the ministers, inspecting sacrificial animals, and nurturing the state elders.

sentences.zh: 十曰象輅，以望秩群祀，視朝，燕諸侯及群臣，燕射，養庶老，適諸侯家，巡省，臨太學，幸道法門。

translations.literal: Tenth, the ivory chariot, for ranking all sacrifices, holding court, banqueting lords and ministers, banquet archery, nurturing common elders, visiting lords' households, touring and inspecting, visiting the Imperial Academy, and visiting the Gate of the Way and Law.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth, the ivory chariot, for ranking all sacrifices, holding court, banqueting lords and ministers, banquet archery, nurturing common elders, visiting lords' households, touring and inspecting, visiting the Imperial Academy, and visiting the Gate of the Way and Law.

sentences.zh: 十一曰革輅，以巡兵即戎。

translations.literal: Eleventh, the leather chariot, for touring the army and going to war.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh, the leather chariot, for touring the army and going to war.

sentences.zh: 十二曰木輅，以田獵，行鄉畿。

translations.literal: Twelfth, the wood chariot, for hunting and traveling the suburban districts.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth, the wood chariot, for hunting and traveling the suburban districts.

sentences.zh: 此六輅，又以六色漆而畫之，用玉碧金象革物以飾諸末。

translations.literal: These six chariots were also lacquered and painted in six colors, using jade, jade-green, gold, ivory, and leather materials to ornament the ends.
translations.idiomatic: These six chariots were also lacquered and painted in six colors, using jade, jade-green, gold, ivory, and leather materials to ornament the ends.

sentences.zh: 皆錫面、金鉤，就以五采，俱十有二。

translations.literal: All had tin faces and gold hooks, with five colors for the ornaments, twelve in all.
translations.idiomatic: All had tin faces and gold hooks, with five colors for the ornaments, twelve in all.

sentences.zh: 錫面，鏤金當顱。

translations.literal: Tin face: gold carved at the forehead.
translations.idiomatic: Tin face: gold carved at the forehead.

sentences.zh: 鉤以屬勒鞶纓。

translations.literal: The hooks attached the bridle and breast ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: The hooks attached the bridle and breast ornaments.

sentences.zh: 皇后之車，亦十二等：一曰重翟，以從皇帝，重翟羽為車蕃祀郊禖，享先皇，朝皇太后。

translations.literal: The empress's carriages also numbered twelve grades: first, the heavy pheasant, for following the emperor; heavy pheasant feathers as carriage ornament for suburban sacrifice to the Gate of Childbirth, feasting the former emperors, and attending the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's carriages also numbered twelve grades: first, the heavy pheasant, for following the emperor; heavy pheasant feathers as carriage ornament for suburban sacrifice to the Gate of Childbirth, feasting the former emperors, and attending the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 二曰厭翟，以祭陰社。

translations.literal: Second, the pressed pheasant, for sacrificing to the Yin altar.
translations.idiomatic: Second, the pressed pheasant, for sacrificing to the Yin altar.

sentences.zh: 次其羽也三曰翟輅，以采桑。

translations.literal: Its feathers ranked below. Third, the pheasant chariot, for mulberry gathering.
translations.idiomatic: Its feathers ranked below. Third, the pheasant chariot, for mulberry gathering.

sentences.zh: 翟羽飾之四曰翠輅，以從皇帝，見賓客。

translations.literal: Ornamented with pheasant feathers. Fourth, the kingfisher chariot, for following the emperor and receiving guests.
translations.idiomatic: Ornamented with pheasant feathers. Fourth, the kingfisher chariot, for following the emperor and receiving guests.

sentences.zh: 翠羽飾之五曰雕輅，以歸寧。

translations.literal: Ornamented with kingfisher feathers. Fifth, the carved chariot, for returning to visit one's parents.
translations.idiomatic: Ornamented with kingfisher feathers. Fifth, the carved chariot, for returning to visit one's parents.

sentences.zh: 刻諸末也六曰篆輅，以臨諸道法門。

translations.literal: Carved ornament on the ends. Sixth, the seal-script chariot, for visiting the various Gates of the Way and Law.
translations.idiomatic: Carved ornament on the ends. Sixth, the seal-script chariot, for visiting the various Gates of the Way and Law.

sentences.zh: 篆諸飾也六輅皆錫面，硃總總以硃絲為之，置馬勒，直兩耳與兩鑣也。

translations.literal: Seal-script ornament. These six chariots all had tin faces; the cinnabar tassel was made of cinnabar silk, placed on the bridle, running straight to both ears and both bits.
translations.idiomatic: Seal-script ornament. These six chariots all had tin faces; the cinnabar tassel was made of cinnabar silk, placed on the bridle, running straight to both ears and both bits.

sentences.zh: 金鉤。

translations.literal: Gold hooks.
translations.idiomatic: Gold hooks.

sentences.zh: 七曰蒼輅，以適命婦家。

translations.literal: Seventh, the dark chariot, for visiting the households of titled ladies.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh, the dark chariot, for visiting the households of titled ladies.

sentences.zh: 八曰青輅，九曰硃輅，十曰黃輅，十一曰白輅，十二曰玄輅。

translations.literal: Eighth, the green chariot; ninth, the cinnabar chariot; tenth, the yellow chariot; eleventh, the white chariot; twelfth, the black chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth, the green chariot; ninth, the cinnabar chariot; tenth, the yellow chariot; eleventh, the white chariot; twelfth, the black chariot.

sentences.zh: 五時常出入則供之。

translations.literal: For the five seasons' regular comings and goings, these were provided.
translations.idiomatic: For the five seasons' regular comings and goings, these were provided.

sentences.zh: 六輅皆疏面，繢總。

translations.literal: The six chariots all had open faces and painted tassels.
translations.idiomatic: The six chariots all had open faces and painted tassels.

sentences.zh: 以畫繒為之

translations.literal: Made of painted silk.
translations.idiomatic: Made of painted silk.

sentences.zh: 諸公之輅九：方輅各象方之色碧輅、金輅，皆錫面，鞶纓九就，金鉤。

translations.literal: The dukes' chariots numbered nine: the directional chariots each represented their directional colors; the jade-green and gold chariots all had tin faces, breast ornaments of nine knots, and gold hooks.
translations.idiomatic: The dukes' chariots numbered nine: the directional chariots each represented their directional colors; the jade-green and gold chariots all had tin faces, breast ornaments of nine knots, and gold hooks.

sentences.zh: 象輅、犀輅、貝輅、革輅、篆輅、木輅，皆疏面，鞶纓九就。

translations.literal: The ivory, rhinoceros, shell, leather, seal-script, and wood chariots all had open faces and breast ornaments of nine knots.
translations.idiomatic: The ivory, rhinoceros, shell, leather, seal-script, and wood chariots all had open faces and breast ornaments of nine knots.

sentences.zh: 凡就，皆以硃白蒼三采。

translations.literal: All knots used the three colors of cinnabar, white, and dark.
translations.idiomatic: All knots used the three colors of cinnabar, white, and dark.

sentences.zh: 諸侯自方輅而下八，又無碧輅。

translations.literal: Marquises from the directional chariot downward had eight, and also lacked the jade-green chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Marquises from the directional chariot downward had eight, and also lacked the jade-green chariot.

sentences.zh: 諸伯自方輅而下七，又無金輅。

translations.literal: Earls from the directional chariot downward had seven, and also lacked the gold chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Earls from the directional chariot downward had seven, and also lacked the gold chariot.

sentences.zh: 諸子自方輅而下六，又無象輅。

translations.literal: Viscounts from the directional chariot downward had six, and also lacked the ivory chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Viscounts from the directional chariot downward had six, and also lacked the ivory chariot.

sentences.zh: 諸男自方輅而下五，又無犀輅。

translations.literal: Barons from the directional chariot downward had five, and also lacked the rhinoceros chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Barons from the directional chariot downward had five, and also lacked the rhinoceros chariot.

sentences.zh: 凡就，各如其命。

translations.literal: All knots corresponded to their rank.
translations.idiomatic: All knots corresponded to their rank.

sentences.zh: 諸公夫人之輅車九：厭翟、翟輅、翠輅，皆錫面，硃總，金鉤。

translations.literal: The ducal consorts' chariots numbered nine: the pressed pheasant, pheasant chariot, and kingfisher chariot all had tin faces, cinnabar tassels, and gold hooks.
translations.idiomatic: The ducal consorts' chariots numbered nine: the pressed pheasant, pheasant chariot, and kingfisher chariot all had tin faces, cinnabar tassels, and gold hooks.

sentences.zh: 雕輅、篆輅，皆勒面，刻白黑韋為當顱繢總。

translations.literal: The carved and seal-script chariots all had bridle faces, with white and black leather carved at the forehead and painted tassels.
translations.idiomatic: The carved and seal-script chariots all had bridle faces, with white and black leather carved at the forehead and painted tassels.

sentences.zh: 硃輅、黃輅、白輅、玄輅，皆雕面，刻漆韋為當顱鷖總。

translations.literal: The cinnabar, yellow, white, and black chariots all had carved faces, with lacquered leather carved at the forehead and duck tassels.
translations.idiomatic: The cinnabar, yellow, white, and black chariots all had carved faces, with lacquered leather carved at the forehead and duck tassels.

sentences.zh: 總青黑色繒，其著如硃總。

translations.literal: The tassel was dark green silk, attached like the cinnabar tassel.
translations.idiomatic: The tassel was dark green silk, attached like the cinnabar tassel.

sentences.zh: 諸侯夫人自翟輅而下八，諸伯夫人自翠輅而下七，諸子夫人自雕輅而下六，諸男夫人自篆輅而下五。

translations.literal: Marquises' consorts from the pheasant chariot downward had eight; earls' consorts from the kingfisher chariot downward had seven; viscounts' consorts from the carved chariot downward had six; barons' consorts from the seal-script chariot downward had five.
translations.idiomatic: Marquises' consorts from the pheasant chariot downward had eight; earls' consorts from the kingfisher chariot downward had seven; viscounts' consorts from the carved chariot downward had six; barons' consorts from the seal-script chariot downward had five.

sentences.zh: 鞶纓就數，各視其君。

translations.literal: The number of breast-ornament knots each followed their lord.
translations.idiomatic: The number of breast-ornament knots each followed their lord.

sentences.zh: 公孤卿大夫，皆以中之色乘祀輅。

translations.literal: The dukes, orphans, ministers, and grand masters all rode the sacrificial chariot in the color of the center.
translations.idiomatic: The dukes, orphans, ministers, and grand masters all rode the sacrificial chariot in the color of the center.

sentences.zh: 士乘祀車。

translations.literal: Knights rode the sacrificial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Knights rode the sacrificial carriage.

sentences.zh: 三公之輅車九：祀輅、犀輅、貝輅、篆輅、木輅、夏篆、夏縵、墨車、晳戔車。

translations.literal: The Three Excellencies' chariots numbered nine: sacrificial chariot, rhinoceros chariot, shell chariot, seal-script chariot, wood chariot, summer seal-script, summer plain, black chariot, and dawn-mist chariot.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Excellencies' chariots numbered nine: sacrificial chariot, rhinoceros chariot, shell chariot, seal-script chariot, wood chariot, summer seal-script, summer plain, black chariot, and dawn-mist chariot.

sentences.zh: 自篆已上，金塗諸末，疏錫，鞶纓，金鉤。

translations.literal: From the seal-script chariot upward, gold plated the ends, open tin, breast ornaments, and gold hooks.
translations.idiomatic: From the seal-script chariot upward, gold plated the ends, open tin, breast ornaments, and gold hooks.

sentences.zh: 木輅已下，銅飾諸末，疏，鞶纓皆九就。

translations.literal: From the wood chariot downward, copper ornamented the ends, open faces, and breast ornaments all had nine knots.
translations.idiomatic: From the wood chariot downward, copper ornamented the ends, open faces, and breast ornaments all had nine knots.

sentences.zh: 三孤自祀輅而下八，無犀輅。

translations.literal: The three orphans from the sacrificial chariot downward had eight, without the rhinoceros chariot.
translations.idiomatic: The three orphans from the sacrificial chariot downward had eight, without the rhinoceros chariot.

sentences.zh: 六卿自祀輅而下七，又無貝輅。

translations.literal: The six ministers from the sacrificial chariot downward had seven, and also lacked the shell chariot.
translations.idiomatic: The six ministers from the sacrificial chariot downward had seven, and also lacked the shell chariot.

sentences.zh: 上大夫自祀輅而下六，又無篆輅。

translations.literal: Senior grand masters from the sacrificial chariot downward had six, and also lacked the seal-script chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Senior grand masters from the sacrificial chariot downward had six, and also lacked the seal-script chariot.

sentences.zh: 中大夫自祀輅而下五，又無木輅。

translations.literal: Middle grand masters from the sacrificial chariot downward had five, and also lacked the wood chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Middle grand masters from the sacrificial chariot downward had five, and also lacked the wood chariot.

sentences.zh: 下大夫自祀輅而下四，又無夏篆。

translations.literal: Junior grand masters from the sacrificial chariot downward had four, and also lacked the summer seal-script.
translations.idiomatic: Junior grand masters from the sacrificial chariot downward had four, and also lacked the summer seal-script.

sentences.zh: 士車三：祀車、墨車、晳戔車。

translations.literal: Knights' carriages numbered three: sacrificial carriage, black carriage, and dawn-mist carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Knights' carriages numbered three: sacrificial carriage, black carriage, and dawn-mist carriage.

sentences.zh: 凡就，各如其命之數。

translations.literal: All knots corresponded to the number of their rank.
translations.idiomatic: All knots corresponded to the number of their rank.

sentences.zh: 自孤下，就以硃綠二采。

translations.literal: From the orphans downward, the knots used the two colors of cinnabar and green.
translations.idiomatic: From the orphans downward, the knots used the two colors of cinnabar and green.

sentences.zh: 三妃、三公夫人之輅九：篆輅、硃輅、黃輅、白輅、玄輅，皆勒面，繢總。

translations.literal: The three consorts and Three Excellencies' consorts' chariots numbered nine: seal-script, cinnabar, yellow, white, and black chariots all had bridle faces and painted tassels.
translations.idiomatic: The three consorts and Three Excellencies' consorts' chariots numbered nine: seal-script, cinnabar, yellow, white, and black chariots all had bridle faces and painted tassels.

sentences.zh: 夏篆、夏縵、墨車、晳戔車，皆雕面，鷖總。

translations.literal: The summer seal-script, summer plain, black carriage, and dawn-mist carriage all had carved faces and duck tassels.
translations.idiomatic: The summer seal-script, summer plain, black carriage, and dawn-mist carriage all had carved faces and duck tassels.

sentences.zh: 三昿弋、三孤內子，自硃輅已下八。

translations.literal: The three secondary consorts and three orphans' inner consorts, from the cinnabar chariot downward had eight.
translations.idiomatic: The three secondary consorts and three orphans' inner consorts, from the cinnabar chariot downward had eight.

sentences.zh: 六嬪、六卿內子，自黃輅而下七。

translations.literal: The six concubines and six ministers' inner consorts, from the yellow chariot downward had seven.
translations.idiomatic: The six concubines and six ministers' inner consorts, from the yellow chariot downward had seven.

sentences.zh: 上媛婦、中大夫孺人，自玄輅而下五。

translations.literal: Senior ladies and middle grand masters' wives, from the black chariot downward had five.
translations.idiomatic: Senior ladies and middle grand masters' wives, from the black chariot downward had five.

sentences.zh: 下媛婦、大夫孺人，自夏篆而下四。

translations.literal: Junior ladies and grand masters' wives, from the summer seal-script downward had four.
translations.idiomatic: Junior ladies and grand masters' wives, from the summer seal-script downward had four.

sentences.zh: 禦婉、士婦人，自夏縵而下三。

translations.literal: Palace attendants and knights' wives, from the summer plain downward had three.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendants and knights' wives, from the summer plain downward had three.

sentences.zh: 其鞶纓就，各以其等。

translations.literal: Their breast-ornament knots each followed their rank.
translations.idiomatic: Their breast-ornament knots each followed their rank.

sentences.zh: 皆簟每笰，漆之。

translations.literal: All had bamboo mats for each seat, lacquered.
translations.idiomatic: All had bamboo mats for each seat, lacquered.

sentences.zh: 君以赤，卿大夫士以玄。

translations.literal: The lord used red; ministers, grand masters, and knights used black.
translations.idiomatic: The lord used red; ministers, grand masters, and knights used black.

sentences.zh: 君駕四，三輈六轡。

translations.literal: The lord drove four, with three shafts and six reins.
translations.idiomatic: The lord drove four, with three shafts and six reins.

sentences.zh: 卿大夫駕三，二輈五轡。

translations.literal: Ministers and grand masters drove three, with two shafts and five reins.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers and grand masters drove three, with two shafts and five reins.

sentences.zh: 士駕二，一輈四轡。

translations.literal: Knights drove two, with one shaft and four reins.
translations.idiomatic: Knights drove two, with one shaft and four reins.

sentences.zh: 輅之制，重輪重較而加耳焉。

translations.literal: The chariot's form: double wheels, double side rails, with ear fittings added.
translations.idiomatic: The chariot's form had double wheels and double side rails, with ear fittings added.

sentences.zh: 皇帝、皇后之輅，輿廣六尺有六寸，輪高七尺。

translations.literal: The emperor's and empress's chariots: the carriage body six chi and six cun wide, wheels seven chi high.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's and empress's chariots: the carriage body was six chi and six cun wide, the wheels seven chi high.

sentences.zh: 畫輪轂、輈衡以雲牙，箱軾以虡文，虡內畫以雜獸。

translations.literal: The painted wheel hubs and shaft crossbars had cloud patterns; the box rails had tiger patterns, and inside the tiger patterns were painted with various beasts.
translations.idiomatic: The painted wheel hubs and shaft crossbars had cloud patterns; the box rails had tiger patterns, and inside the tiger patterns various beasts were painted.

sentences.zh: 獸伏軾，倚較。

translations.literal: Beasts recumbent on the front rail, leaning side rails.
translations.idiomatic: Beasts recumbent on the front rail and leaning side rails.

sentences.zh: 諸侯及夫人、命夫、命婦之輅車，廣六尺有二寸，輪崇六尺有六寸。

translations.literal: The chariots of lords and their consorts, titled husbands, and titled wives: six chi and two cun wide, wheels six chi and six cun high.
translations.idiomatic: The chariots of lords and their consorts, titled husbands, and titled wives were six chi and two cun wide, with wheels six chi and six cun high.

sentences.zh: 畫轂以雲牙，軾以虡文，虡內畫以雲華。

translations.literal: The hubs were painted with cloud patterns; the rails with tiger patterns; inside the tiger patterns were painted with cloud flowers.
translations.idiomatic: The hubs were painted with cloud patterns; the rails with tiger patterns; inside the tiger patterns cloud flowers were painted.

sentences.zh: 倚較。

translations.literal: Leaning side rails.
translations.idiomatic: They had leaning side rails.

sentences.zh: 士不畫。

translations.literal: Knights had no painting.
translations.idiomatic: Knights' carriages had no painting.

sentences.zh: 後、夫人、內子已下，同去獸與鹿。

translations.literal: From the empress, consorts, and inner consorts downward, beasts and deer were alike removed.
translations.idiomatic: From the empress, consorts, and inner consorts downward, beasts and deer were alike removed.

sentences.zh: 凡旗，太常畫三辰，日、月、五星。

translations.literal: For all banners: the Grand Standard was painted with the three luminaries—sun, moon, and five planets.
translations.idiomatic: For all banners: the Grand Standard was painted with the three luminaries—sun, moon, and five planets.

sentences.zh: 旃畫青龍皇帝升龍，諸侯交龍。

translations.literal: The zhan banner was painted with the azure dragon; the emperor's ascending dragon, the lords' interlaced dragons.
translations.idiomatic: The zhan banner was painted with the azure dragon—the emperor's ascending dragon and the lords' interlaced dragons.

sentences.zh: 旟畫硃雀，旌畫黃麟，旗畫白獸，旐畫玄武，皆加雲。

translations.literal: The yu banner was painted with the vermilion bird; the jing banner with the yellow qilin; the qi banner with the white beast; the zhao banner with the dark warrior—all with clouds added.
translations.idiomatic: The yu banner was painted with the vermilion bird; the jing banner with the yellow qilin; the qi banner with the white beast; the zhao banner with the dark warrior—all with clouds added.

sentences.zh: 其旃物在軍，亦書其事號，加之以雲氣。

translations.literal: Their banner emblems in the army also recorded their affair designations, with cloud vapor added.
translations.idiomatic: Their banner emblems in the army also recorded their affair designations, with cloud vapor added.

sentences.zh: 徽幟亦如之。

translations.literal: Insignia banners were the same.
translations.idiomatic: Insignia banners were the same.

sentences.zh: 通帛為旃，雜帛為物。

translations.literal: Plain silk made the zhan; mixed silk made the emblems.
translations.idiomatic: Plain silk made the zhan; mixed silk made the emblems.

sentences.zh: 在軍亦書其人官與姓名之事號。

translations.literal: In the army they also recorded the person's office and name and affair designation.
translations.idiomatic: In the army they also recorded the person's office, name, and affair designation.

sentences.zh: 徽幟亦書之，但畫其所書之例。

translations.literal: Insignia banners also recorded these, but painted according to what was written.
translations.idiomatic: Insignia banners also recorded these, but painted according to what was written.

sentences.zh: 旌節又畫白獸，而析羽於其上。

translations.literal: Command batons also painted the white beast, with split feathers on top.
translations.idiomatic: Command batons also painted the white beast, with split feathers on top.

sentences.zh: 司常，掌旗物之藏。

translations.literal: The Director of Standards managed the storage of banner emblems.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Standards managed the storage of banner emblems.

sentences.zh: 通帛之旗六，以供郊丘之祀。

translations.literal: Plain-silk banners numbered six, for supplying suburban and mound sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Plain-silk banners numbered six, for supplying suburban and mound sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 一曰蒼旗，二曰青旗，三曰硃旗，四曰黃旗，五曰白旗，六曰玄旗。

translations.literal: First, the dark banner; second, the green banner; third, the cinnabar banner; fourth, the yellow banner; fifth, the white banner; sixth, the black banner.
translations.idiomatic: First, the dark banner; second, the green banner; third, the cinnabar banner; fourth, the yellow banner; fifth, the white banner; sixth, the black banner.

sentences.zh: 畫繢之旗六，以充玉輅之等。

translations.literal: Painted banners numbered six, to supply the jade chariot grades.
translations.idiomatic: Painted banners numbered six, to supply the jade chariot grades.

sentences.zh: 一曰三辰之常，二曰青龍之旗，三曰硃鳥之旟，四曰黃麟之旌，五曰白獸之旗，六曰玄武之旐。

translations.literal: First, the three-luminaries standard; second, the azure dragon banner; third, the vermilion bird yu; fourth, the yellow qilin jing; fifth, the white beast qi; sixth, the dark warrior zhao.
translations.idiomatic: First, the three-luminaries standard; second, the azure dragon banner; third, the vermilion bird yu; fourth, the yellow qilin jing; fifth, the white beast qi; sixth, the dark warrior zhao.

sentences.zh: 皆左建旗而右建闟戟。

translations.literal: All had banners erected on the left and halberd-shields on the right.
translations.idiomatic: All had banners erected on the left and halberd-shields on the right.

sentences.zh: 又有繼旗四，以施軍旅。

translations.literal: There were also four relay banners for use in military campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: There were also four relay banners for use in military campaigns.

sentences.zh: 一曰麾，以供軍將。

translations.literal: First, the command banner, for army generals.
translations.idiomatic: First, the command banner, for army generals.

sentences.zh: 二曰Ｋ，以供師帥。

translations.literal: Second, the signal banner, for division commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Second, the signal banner, for division commanders.

sentences.zh: 三曰枿，以供旅帥。

translations.literal: Third, the regimental banner, for brigade commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Third, the regimental banner, for brigade commanders.

sentences.zh: 四曰旆，以供倅長。

translations.literal: Fourth, the pennant, for company leaders.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, the pennant, for company leaders.

sentences.zh: 諸公方輅、碧輅建旂，金輅建旟，象輅建物，木輅建旐。

translations.literal: The dukes' directional and jade-green chariots flew qi banners; the gold chariot flew yu; the ivory chariot flew emblems; the wood chariot flew zhao.
translations.idiomatic: The dukes' directional and jade-green chariots flew qi banners; the gold chariot flew yu; the ivory chariot flew emblems; the wood chariot flew zhao.

sentences.zh: 諸侯自金輅而下，如諸公之旗。

translations.literal: Marquises from the gold chariot downward followed the dukes' banners.
translations.idiomatic: Marquises from the gold chariot downward followed the dukes' banners.

sentences.zh: 諸伯自象輅而下，如諸侯之旗。

translations.literal: Earls from the ivory chariot downward followed the marquises' banners.
translations.idiomatic: Earls from the ivory chariot downward followed the marquises' banners.

sentences.zh: 諸子自犀輅而下，如諸伯之旗。

translations.literal: Viscounts from the rhinoceros chariot downward followed the earls' banners.
translations.idiomatic: Viscounts from the rhinoceros chariot downward followed the earls' banners.

sentences.zh: 諸男自象輅而下，如諸子之旗。

translations.literal: Barons from the ivory chariot downward followed the viscounts' banners.
translations.idiomatic: Barons from the ivory chariot downward followed the viscounts' banners.

sentences.zh: 三公犀輅、貝輅、篆輅建旃，木輅建旐，夏篆、夏縵及晳戔車建物。

translations.literal: The Three Excellencies' rhinoceros, shell, and seal-script chariots flew zhan; the wood chariot flew zhao; the summer seal-script, summer plain, and dawn-mist carriages flew emblems.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Excellencies' rhinoceros, shell, and seal-script chariots flew zhan; the wood chariot flew zhao; the summer seal-script, summer plain, and dawn-mist carriages flew emblems.

sentences.zh: 孤卿已下，各以其等建其旗。

translations.literal: Orphans and ministers downward each flew banners according to their rank.
translations.idiomatic: Orphans and ministers downward each flew banners according to their rank.

sentences.zh: 旌杠，皇帝六刃，諸侯五刃，大夫四刃，士三刃。

translations.literal: Banner poles: the emperor six blades; lords five blades; grand masters four blades; knights three blades.
translations.idiomatic: Banner poles: the emperor six blades; lords five blades; grand masters four blades; knights three blades.

sentences.zh: 旒，皇帝曳地，諸侯及軹，大夫及轂，士及軫。

translations.literal: Tassels: the emperor's trailed on the ground; lords' reached the wheel hubs; grand masters' reached the wheel spokes; knights' reached the wheel rims.
translations.idiomatic: Tassels: the emperor's trailed on the ground; lords' reached the wheel hubs; grand masters' reached the wheel spokes; knights' reached the wheel rims.

sentences.zh: 凡注毛於杠首曰綏，析羽曰旌，全羽曰Ｋ。

translations.literal: All feathers attached to the pole top were called tassels; split feathers made jing; whole feathers made signal banners.
translations.idiomatic: All feathers attached to the pole top were called tassels; split feathers made jing; whole feathers made signal banners.

sentences.zh: 其幓，皇帝諸侯加以弧韣。

translations.literal: Their streamers: the emperor and lords added bow cases.
